extractions.value: The paper describes a case of Borrelia burgdorferi myelitis presenting as a partial stiff man syndrome, with symptoms confined to the left leg. The authors suggest the process is within the spinal grey matter, possibly affecting spinal interneurons. They note that B. burgdorferi is able to induce autoreactive T cells and autoantibodies specific for brain antigens, suggesting an autoimmune mechanism may be involved.
extractions.quote: the process might be tentatively considered to be within the spinal grey matter. ... B. burgdorferi, is able to induce autoreactive T cells and autoantibodies specific for brain antigens. Therefore, the spinal cord disturbances could have been mediated either by the spirochaete itself or by the above-mentioned autoimmune process.
